evidence.title: An Improved Fixed Switching Frequency Direct Torque Control of Induction Motor Drives Fed by Direct Matrix Converter
evidence.abstract: A few papers have been interested by the fixed switching frequency direct torque control fed by direct matrix converters, where we can find just the use of direct torque controlled space vector modulated method. In this present paper, we present an improved method used for a fixed switching frequency direct torque control (DTC) using a direct matrix converter (DMC). This method is characterized by a simple structure, a fixed switching frequency which causes minimal torque ripple and a unity input power factor. Using this strategy, we combine the direct matrix converters advantages with those of direct torque control (DTC) schemes. The used technique for constant frequency is combined with the input current space vector to create the switching table of direct matrix converter (DMC). Simulation results clearly demonstrate a better dynamic and steady state performances of the proposed method.

evidence.title: Reconstructing the intermittent dynamics of the torque in wind turbines
evidence.abstract: We apply a framework introduced in the late nineties to analyze load measurements in off-shore wind energy converters (WEC). The framework is borrowed from statistical physics and properly adapted to the analysis of multivariate data comprising wind velocity, power production and torque measurements, taken at one single WEC. In particular, we assume that wind statistics drives the fluctuations of the torque produced in the wind turbine and show how to extract an evolution equation of the Langevin type for the torque driven by the wind velocity. It is known that the intermittent nature of the atmosphere, i.e. of the wind field, is transferred to the power production of a wind energy converter and consequently to the shaft torque. We show that the derived stochastic differential equation quantifies the dynamical coupling of the measured fluctuating properties as well as it reproduces the intermittency observed in the data. Finally, we discuss our approach in the light of turbine monitoring, a particular important issue in off-shore wind farms.

evidence.title: A Finite State and Rule-based Akshara to Prosodeme (A2P) Converter in Hindi
evidence.abstract: This article describes a software module called Akshara to Prosodeme (A2P) converter in Hindi. It converts an input grapheme into prosedeme (sequence of phonemes with the specification of syllable boundaries and prosodic labels). The software is based on two proposed finite state machines\textemdash one for the syllabification and another for the syllable labeling. In addition to that, it also uses a set of nonlinear phonological rules proposed for foot formation in Hindi, which encompass solutions to schwa-deletion in simple, compound, derived and inflected words. The nonlinear phonological rules are based on metrical phonology with the provision of recursive foot structure. A software module is implemented in Python. The testing of the software for syllabification, syllable labeling, schwa deletion and prosodic labeling yield an accuracy of more than 99% on a lexicon of size 28664 words.

evidence.title: Anti‐shudder durability of automatic transmission fluids: Mechanism of the loss of shudder control
evidence.abstract: Abstract Field samples of automatic transmission fluid (ATF) from vehicles fitted with controlled‐slip torque converter clutches have been analysed to determine the cause of the onset of vehicle shudder. A laboratory anti‐shudder test has been developed using the SAE No. 2 machine. This test includes several degradation mechanisms: thermal degradation in engaging clutches, oxidative degradation in the presence of catalytic metals, and degradation produced by a continuously sliding clutch. At least in the case of one specific fluid, the mode of failure produced in the laboratory test was very similar to the mode of failure in the vehicle. Fluids with improved anti‐shudder durability have been evaluated by this test method and fail by different mechanisms. Test matrices have been conducted to separate the contribution of fluid and hardware to the loss of shudder control in these systems.

evidence.title: Interaction Between ATFs and Friction Material for Modulated Torque Converter Clutches
evidence.abstract: Automatic transmissions equipped with Modulated Torque Converter Clutches (MTCC) require an effective combination of automatic transmission fluid (ATF) - friction material in order to maintain frictional integrity. However, in this study, thermal analysis has shown that ATFs can interact chemically with a friction material used in the MTCC under service conditions, potentially affecting the frictional characteristics. A technique was developed to evaluate friction material degradation. The results of this study showed that the friction material my be chemically altered by static aging in certain ATFs at elevated temperatures. The statically aged friction material samples exhibited thermal analysis signatures which were similar to identical material degraded during dynamometer and fleet vehicle tests. These vehicle tests resulted in deterioration in friction characteristics and experienced shudder. In contrast, an ATF with which the friction material was shown to be relatively inert demonstrated excellent anti-shudder performance in both dynamometer and vehicle durability tests. This suggests that the interaction between ATFs and friction material my contribute significantly to the degradation of friction material systems and the performance of the MTCC.

evidence.title: ATF Bulk Oxidative Degradation and Its Effects on LVFA Friction and the Performance of a Modulated Torque Converter Clutch
evidence.abstract: The friction behaviors of fresh and aged ATFs and a paper-based wet friction material were characterized using a low velocity friction apparatus (LVFA). Friction tests on 30 ml samples of ATF were used to characterize the friction durability of ATFs aged in test vehicles and in the Ford Aluminum Beaker Oxidation Test (ABOT). Oxidation test data gave stability rankings for the various ATFs which were consistent with limited vehicle experience. The procedure was applied to the analysis of results from a fleet test run with transmissions equipped with a modulated torque converter clutch. The test was aimed at characterizing friction degradation and shudder. Samples obtained from the test fleet were used to construct degradation profiles for two ATFs. The profiles showed no significant difference between the two ATFs in friction stability, consistent with the results of bench oxidation tests. However, an oil to air cooler was seen to provide some improvement. A friction coefficient - speed slope criterion was proposed as an indicator for an ATF prone to cause shudder. ABOT tests were carried out on one fluid at several different temperatures. Samples were withdrawn periodically and run in the LVFA. Time-temperature degradation profiles were constructed from the friction data and used to make quantitative predictions of friction degradation in the test vehicles. The results agreed well, supporting the idea that bulk oxidative degradation of ATF in service is a key factor in friction durability of modulated torque converter clutches.

mechanism_map.mechanism: Torsional vibration damper integrated within a hydrodynamic torque converter, using a turbine hub coaxially arranged with the rotating shaft and non-rotatably fixed to the turbine wheel, so torsional oscillations transmitted between the turbine and the output shaft are absorbed by the damper stage rather than passed into the driveline.
mechanism_map.intervention: Retrofit or service-fit a torsional vibration damper assembly into the torque converter of the 2020 Toyota Camry's automatic transmission, anchoring the damper stage to a turbine hub fixed non-rotatably to the turbine wheel, with damper springs/hysteresis elements tuned to the engine's torsional excitation order and the lock-up clutch shudder frequency band.
mechanism_map.expected_effect: Torsional excitation from the engine and lock-up clutch slip is damped before reaching the transmission input shaft, reducing the resonant torsional vibration that manifests as torque converter shudder and vehicle vibration, with improved durability under high-mileage service.
mechanism_map.falsification_test: On a transmission dynamometer or vehicle road test with torsional accelerometers on the input shaft, compare vibration amplitude at the shudder frequency (typically ~20-60 Hz under lock-up clutch slip) before and after damper installation; the mechanism is falsified if torsional amplitude and vehicle vibration are not reduced by a statistically significant margin, or if the damper stage fails fatigue life targets (e.g., < full high-mileage service interval) under cyclic torsional loading.

system.value: An Improved Fixed Switching Frequency Direct Torque Control of Induction Motor Drives Fed by Direct Matrix Converter

abstract.value: A few papers have been interested by the fixed switching frequency direct torque control fed by direct matrix converters, where we can find just the use of direct torque controlled space vector modulated method. In this present paper, we present an improved method used for a fixed switching frequency direct torque control (DTC) using a direct matrix converter (DMC). This method is characterized by a simple structure, a fixed switching frequency which causes minimal torque ripple and a unity input power factor. Using this strategy, we combine the direct matrix converters advantages with those of direct torque control (DTC) schemes. The used technique for constant frequency is combined with the input current space vector to create the switching table of direct matrix converter (DMC). Simulation results clearly demonstrate a better dynamic and steady state performances of the proposed method.

system.value: Reconstructing the intermittent dynamics of the torque in wind turbines

abstract.value: We apply a framework introduced in the late nineties to analyze load measurements in off-shore wind energy converters (WEC). The framework is borrowed from statistical physics and properly adapted to the analysis of multivariate data comprising wind velocity, power production and torque measurements, taken at one single WEC. In particular, we assume that wind statistics drives the fluctuations of the torque produced in the wind turbine and show how to extract an evolution equation of the Langevin type for the torque driven by the wind velocity. It is known that the intermittent nature of the atmosphere, i.e. of the wind field, is transferred to the power production of a wind energy converter and consequently to the shaft torque. We show that the derived stochastic differential equation quantifies the dynamical coupling of the measured fluctuating properties as well as it reproduces the intermittency observed in the data. Finally, we discuss our approach in the light of turbine monitoring, a particular important issue in off-shore wind farms.

system.value: Anti‐shudder durability of automatic transmission fluids: Mechanism of the loss of shudder control

abstract.value: Abstract Field samples of automatic transmission fluid (ATF) from vehicles fitted with controlled‐slip torque converter clutches have been analysed to determine the cause of the onset of vehicle shudder. A laboratory anti‐shudder test has been developed using the SAE No. 2 machine. This test includes several degradation mechanisms: thermal degradation in engaging clutches, oxidative degradation in the presence of catalytic metals, and degradation produced by a continuously sliding clutch. At least in the case of one specific fluid, the mode of failure produced in the laboratory test was very similar to the mode of failure in the vehicle. Fluids with improved anti‐shudder durability have been evaluated by this test method and fail by different mechanisms. Test matrices have been conducted to separate the contribution of fluid and hardware to the loss of shudder control in these systems.

system.value: Mechanism of Shudder Phenomena in Torque Converter and System Simulation Model

abstract.value: It has been past over 10 years since the slip-controlled clutch has adopted to torque converters as improvement technology of fuel consumption. In the recent trend, the updated demand is use of expanded slipping control for further improvement of the transmission efficiency. However, there are the cases of vibration issues in slip-controlled torque converter clutches. This issue is called shudder as typical problem of vehicle vibration. In design of torque converter, it is known as the importance to manage μ -V property preventing from shudder vibration. However, it was difficult to predict μ -V property on the actual system, because of its complex interface phenomena are caused by various changeable factors include physical and chemical. Therefore, if prototype design was never satisfied anti- shudder properties, we need to change design and lost much time to redesign it. In this paper, we report a new technology of predicting μ -V property on torque converter clutch (TCC) using simulation model and μ-V property with the interface phenomena of the Elasto-hydrodynamic Lubrication (EHL) in TCC system.

system.value: Interaction Between ATFs and Friction Material for Modulated Torque Converter Clutches

abstract.value: Automatic transmissions equipped with Modulated Torque Converter Clutches (MTCC) require an effective combination of automatic transmission fluid (ATF) - friction material in order to maintain frictional integrity. However, in this study, thermal analysis has shown that ATFs can interact chemically with a friction material used in the MTCC under service conditions, potentially affecting the frictional characteristics. A technique was developed to evaluate friction material degradation. The results of this study showed that the friction material my be chemically altered by static aging in certain ATFs at elevated temperatures. The statically aged friction material samples exhibited thermal analysis signatures which were similar to identical material degraded during dynamometer and fleet vehicle tests. These vehicle tests resulted in deterioration in friction characteristics and experienced shudder. In contrast, an ATF with which the friction material was shown to be relatively inert demonstrated excellent anti-shudder performance in both dynamometer and vehicle durability tests. This suggests that the interaction between ATFs and friction material my contribute significantly to the degradation of friction material systems and the performance of the MTCC.

cemetery_warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

informational.mechanism: RES-4 narrow: adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent for CSF absorption regulation via AG pressure gradient control
informational.lesson: MODEL-BOUNDED NEGATIVE RESULT: Before inventing variable geometry, calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point. Relative r^4 sensitivity is meaningless if the absolute pressure drop is tiny. Under realistic post-stenting conditions (D=5-10mm, Q=200-500 mL/min), adaptive diameter control of a venous sinus produces <0.2 mmHg change in AG gradient — 5x below the 1 mmHg pre-registered threshold. Control authority exists only in the stenotic+high-flow regime (D≤4mm, Q≥1200 mL/min), which is incompatible with a stented patient whose stent has normalized diameter to 7-10mm. The network model (1323 configs) confirms: flow redistribution through contralateral sinus does NOT rescue control authority (dominance has no effect). NOT a universal vascular invariant — based on Poiseuille model with specific assumptions about geometry, flow, and topology.

informational.mechanism: Minimum Sufficient Validation Evidence Derivation (MSVED) — 4-link chain: ML change → clinical pathway → risk envelope → minimum sufficient evidence → sufficiency proof
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-019: A clinical-pathway-aware evidence selector must demonstrate that the clinical-pathway bridge produces a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than information-maximizing selection (BOED). If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. The minimum-evidence claim must be validated by showing tests_required < BOED, not just tests_required < conventional. The killer experiment must compare against the STRONGEST available baseline (BOED), not just conventional full-validation.

informational.mechanism: Automated Sufficiency Proof Generator (CC-04 / MSES theorem) — formal proof that a specific evidence set E is sufficient to establish modification-specific clinical risk envelope R(Δ)
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).

informational.mechanism: Non-Inferiority Statistical Engine (CC-08) — automated paired NI comparison with pre-registered margins for ML model modifications
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-021: Automating a standard statistical test (NI testing) for a regulatory context that explicitly requires it (PCCP) is NOT an invention. Under KSR, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is obvious. The coder correctly identified this in the R254 ranking ("NI testing is standard, high collision risk") but incorrectly chose to proceed. The CEO corrected: high collision risk is a RED FLAG, not a reason to proceed. Kill immediately if the smallest surviving mechanism is standard statistics + ML context + automated reporting.

informational.mechanism: SGET (Strain-Gated Electrochemical Transduction) — A=strain pulse changes B=electrochemical sensor from 2D surface to 3D depth profiling. First synergy-2 candidate.
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.

informational.mechanism: SC-05 Biofilm-Resistant Living-Surface Venous Interface — continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface with active surface-energy control at CSF-blood interface
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-023: A candidate that survives the 14-gate protocol at the CONCEPT level can be killed at the ELEMENT-DECOMPOSITION level. The 14 gates assessed M4 against the broad concept (continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface) and found M4=NOT FOUND. But deep collision revealed that each element (continuous renewal, dynamic topography, surface-energy modulation) is individually occupied by prior art. The combination is an aggregation of known anti-fouling approaches. The lesson: M4 must be assessed at the ELEMENT level, not the concept level. And M4=NOT FOUND means the search has not found comparable performance yet — not that it does not exist.

custody_records.raw_content: We apply a framework introduced in the late nineties to analyze load measurements in off-shore wind energy converters (WEC). The framework is borrowed from statistical physics and properly adapted to the analysis of multivariate data comprising wind velocity, power production and torque measurements, taken at one single WEC. In particular, we assume that wind statistics drives the fluctuations of the torque produced in the wind turbine and show how to extract an evolution equation of the Langevin type for the torque driven by the wind velocity. It is known that the intermittent nature of the atmosphere, i.e. of the wind field, is transferred to the power production of a wind energy converter and consequently to the shaft torque. We show that the derived stochastic differential equation quantifies the dynamical coupling of the measured fluctuating properties as well as it reproduces the intermittency observed in the data. Finally, we discuss our approach in the light of turbine monitoring, a particular important issue in off-shore wind farms.

custody_records.raw_content: This article describes a software module called Akshara to Prosodeme (A2P) converter in Hindi. It converts an input grapheme into prosedeme (sequence of phonemes with the specification of syllable boundaries and prosodic labels). The software is based on two proposed finite state machines\textemdash one for the syllabification and another for the syllable labeling. In addition to that, it also uses a set of nonlinear phonological rules proposed for foot formation in Hindi, which encompass solutions to schwa-deletion in simple, compound, derived and inflected words. The nonlinear phonological rules are based on metrical phonology with the provision of recursive foot structure. A software module is implemented in Python. The testing of the software for syllabification, syllable labeling, schwa deletion and prosodic labeling yield an accuracy of more than 99% on a lexicon of size 28664 words.

custody_records.raw_content: Abstract Field samples of automatic transmission fluid (ATF) from vehicles fitted with controlled‐slip torque converter clutches have been analysed to determine the cause of the onset of vehicle shudder. A laboratory anti‐shudder test has been developed using the SAE No. 2 machine. This test includes several degradation mechanisms: thermal degradation in engaging clutches, oxidative degradation in the presence of catalytic metals, and degradation produced by a continuously sliding clutch. At least in the case of one specific fluid, the mode of failure produced in the laboratory test was very similar to the mode of failure in the vehicle. Fluids with improved anti‐shudder durability have been evaluated by this test method and fail by different mechanisms. Test matrices have been conducted to separate the contribution of fluid and hardware to the loss of shudder control in these systems.

custody_records.raw_content: It has been past over 10 years since the slip-controlled clutch has adopted to torque converters as improvement technology of fuel consumption. In the recent trend, the updated demand is use of expanded slipping control for further improvement of the transmission efficiency. However, there are the cases of vibration issues in slip-controlled torque converter clutches. This issue is called shudder as typical problem of vehicle vibration. In design of torque converter, it is known as the importance to manage μ -V property preventing from shudder vibration. However, it was difficult to predict μ -V property on the actual system, because of its complex interface phenomena are caused by various changeable factors include physical and chemical. Therefore, if prototype design was never satisfied anti- shudder properties, we need to change design and lost much time to redesign it. In this paper, we report a new technology of predicting μ -V property on torque converter clutch (TCC) using simulation model and μ-V property with the interface phenomena of the Elasto-hydrodynamic Lubrication (EHL) in TCC system.

custody_records.raw_content: Automatic transmissions equipped with Modulated Torque Converter Clutches (MTCC) require an effective combination of automatic transmission fluid (ATF) - friction material in order to maintain frictional integrity. However, in this study, thermal analysis has shown that ATFs can interact chemically with a friction material used in the MTCC under service conditions, potentially affecting the frictional characteristics. A technique was developed to evaluate friction material degradation. The results of this study showed that the friction material my be chemically altered by static aging in certain ATFs at elevated temperatures. The statically aged friction material samples exhibited thermal analysis signatures which were similar to identical material degraded during dynamometer and fleet vehicle tests. These vehicle tests resulted in deterioration in friction characteristics and experienced shudder. In contrast, an ATF with which the friction material was shown to be relatively inert demonstrated excellent anti-shudder performance in both dynamometer and vehicle durability tests. This suggests that the interaction between ATFs and friction material my contribute significantly to the degradation of friction material systems and the performance of the MTCC.

custody_records.raw_content: The friction behaviors of fresh and aged ATFs and a paper-based wet friction material were characterized using a low velocity friction apparatus (LVFA). Friction tests on 30 ml samples of ATF were used to characterize the friction durability of ATFs aged in test vehicles and in the Ford Aluminum Beaker Oxidation Test (ABOT). Oxidation test data gave stability rankings for the various ATFs which were consistent with limited vehicle experience. The procedure was applied to the analysis of results from a fleet test run with transmissions equipped with a modulated torque converter clutch. The test was aimed at characterizing friction degradation and shudder. Samples obtained from the test fleet were used to construct degradation profiles for two ATFs. The profiles showed no significant difference between the two ATFs in friction stability, consistent with the results of bench oxidation tests. However, an oil to air cooler was seen to provide some improvement. A friction coefficient - speed slope criterion was proposed as an indicator for an ATF prone to cause shudder. ABOT tests were carried out on one fluid at several different temperatures. Samples were withdrawn periodically and run in the LVFA. Time-temperature degradation profiles were constructed from the friction data and used to make quantitative predictions of friction degradation in the test vehicles. The results agreed well, supporting the idea that bulk oxidative degradation of ATF in service is a key factor in friction durability of modulated torque converter clutches.
